title: Masterplan rebuild from a neutral rebuild package: floors, DirectShape envelopes and domain-based grids (incl. arcs) via the Revit API
license_confirmation: I wrote this or have the right to share it, and I agree to publish it under CC BY 4.0 (text/JSON) and MIT (code).

context.tool_or_bridge: RevitBridge MCP (run_csharp, Roslyn 4.8 / C# 12); payload files written to the user's computer and read by Revit from disk; desktop screenshots and Revit image export for visual checks
context.project_type: healthcare campus masterplan (the contributor's own design), concept

intent: Rebuild a 13-building masterplan in an empty Revit project from a compact, tool-neutral rebuild package (levels, 22 floor-profile prototypes placed as 48 floors, 13 exact mass envelopes as triangle face loops) and then create structural/reference grids per building, without re-reading the original SketchUp source and without inventing walls, rooms or structure.
use_when: A neutral package of levels, floor profiles and exact envelopes must become native Revit elements
Exact source mass geometry (triangle face loops) has to enter Revit as DirectShape
Grids must be created for many buildings at once, including rotated wings and curved (arc) buildings
A payload is too large to embed in a code-execution call
not_for: Reading or interpreting the original source model (that is the upstream USG intake)
Structural design: grid intersections are column-centreline candidates only
api_terms: Arc.Create(center, radius, startAngle, endAngle, xAxis, yAxis)

usage_report.tool_calls: Rebuild: 9 Revit calls (levels 1, floors 1, envelopes 5 incl. 3 failed + 2 rolled-back dry runs, STK-09 envelope 1, review view 2). Grids v1: 1 build + 2 read-backs. Grids v2: 1 replace + 1 read-back/export + 1 view + 1 export. About 4.6 s of Revit execution in successful build calls.
usage_report.retries: 3 failed envelope calls (wrong API member; a single-read result read twice); 1 verification read-back that found 0 grids (silent tag failure); 1 image export of a cropped template view

packs.why: Staging, idempotent tags, Mark/Comments evidence tags and the visual gate were reused as written. Adapted for a masterplan: stages became levels -> floors -> envelopes -> grids; the visual gate used Revit image export of a dedicated uncropped view instead of driving the UI; the version gate (rule 5) was not applied up front for TessellatedShapeBuilder and cost two failed calls (see iterations).

usage_report.without_arpl_estimate: Rule 5 of ARPL-GEO-0004 (reflect the API before non-trivial members) would have prevented 2 of the 3 failed envelope calls had it been followed for TessellatedShapeBuilderResult.

iterations.instruction: Embed the build data in the C# snippet.
iterations.result: Not attempted for envelopes: the largest envelope was 200 KB (5,907 triangles).
iterations.problem: Inline payloads that large are error-prone to pass through a code tool.
iterations.found_by: payload size check before the build

iterations.instruction: Write the payload JSON files to a folder on the user's computer (one-time folder approval) and read them in Revit with File.ReadAllText + JObject.Parse.
iterations.result: Worked for all stages; 15 files, read in milliseconds.

iterations.instruction: Create 48 floors with Floor.Create, one call, each in a SubTransaction; 9 profiles have two disjoint regions, passed as two CurveLoops to one Floor.Create.
iterations.result: 48/48 created in 2.1 s; multi-region floors created as single elements; total area 3,134,736 sq ft equals the package; max per-floor deviation 0.001 sq ft (HOST_AREA_COMPUTED vs shoelace area of the source).
iterations.problem: None. A Revit floor always has thickness; the owner chose the template's 'Generic - 12"' as a tagged stand-in.
iterations.found_by: area comparison in the same call

iterations.instruction: Build 12 envelopes with TessellatedShapeBuilder; log r.GetNumberOfIssues(); set ds.Name; read r.GetGeometricalObjects() for SetShape and again for volume.
iterations.result: Compile error: GetNumberOfIssues does not exist. Then runtime InvalidOperationException with no message, twice.
iterations.problem: Method assumed from memory (FP40). GetGeometricalObjects() can be read only once per build result; the second read throws. (The DirectShape.Name setter was a first suspect; SetName() is the method to use.)
iterations.found_by: rolled-back dry run with step markers, then a per-file dry run in try/catch that showed every build succeeding up to SetShape

iterations.instruction: Read GetGeometricalObjects() once into a variable; use ds.SetName(); Target AnyGeometry, Fallback Mesh.
iterations.result: 12 envelopes in 48 ms, STK-09 (5,907 triangles) in 372 ms. Outcomes: 10 Solid, 2 Mesh, 1 Sheet. Bounding boxes match the source exactly; volumes of the 10 solids match the source signed volume to the cubic foot.
iterations.problem: The Mesh/Sheet outcomes are not adapter errors: an edge-count check of the source triangles found 1 and 2 non-manifold edges (Mesh) and 1,069 open edges (Sheet). A Sheet's volume is not meaningful.
iterations.found_by: per-envelope Outcome, then an edge-use count (edges used once = open, more than twice = non-manifold) on the source data

iterations.instruction: Create 261 grids from the package's CSV (bounding-box grids per building); tag each with Comments; verify by reading back grids whose Comments start with the tag.
iterations.result: 261 created in 0.9 s, but the read-back found 0 grids.
iterations.problem: Grid datums have no ALL_MODEL_INSTANCE_COMMENTS parameter; the write used get_Parameter(...)?.Set(...), so the null-conditional silently skipped every tag. Separately, the owner's test case rejected the bounding-box grids: floors of three narrow wings extended 17.6-50.6 ft beyond their grids.
iterations.found_by: read-back count; floor-vs-grid coverage check in the building's grid frame

iterations.instruction: Replace with domain-based grids (one grid domain per wing, standard bays with rational end bays, a curved building as radial lines plus concentric arcs): delete the 261 grids and create 361 (357 lines, 4 arcs) in one transaction, then read back by name prefix.
iterations.result: 361/361 in 1.3 s, one undo step; read-back by name: names unique, 4 arcs are Arc curves, line endpoints and arc radii/centres at 0.0 ft deviation; 0 grids cross another building, 0 run into another wing of the same building.
iterations.problem: Deleting first in the same transaction avoids name clashes with the old grids (same naming scheme). Grid heads crowd where several wings meet; per-building scope boxes would fix this, but scope boxes cannot be created through the Revit API.
iterations.found_by: read-back; image export of a plan view

iterations.instruction: Visual check: bring Revit to the front with the desktop-control open-application call and press ZF.
iterations.result: A second, empty Revit 2024 instance started (splash screen); the model stayed in the first instance, which the bridge kept using.
iterations.problem: Opening an already-running desktop application can launch a new instance instead of focusing the running one.
iterations.found_by: screenshot showing the splash; bridge status listing two live Revit sessions

iterations.instruction: Visual check without the UI: Document.ExportImage of the template's ground-floor plan.
iterations.result: The image showed only a small corner near the origin.
iterations.problem: The template plan view had an active crop region.
iterations.found_by: looking at the exported image; fixed by creating a dedicated plan view with CropBoxActive = false, no template, elevation/section/mass categories hidden, and exporting that

final_rule.lesson: A neutral rebuild package becomes native Revit quickly and exactly when data travels as files, every element is identified by name or Mark (not by a parameter that may not exist), envelopes are pre-checked for closure, and visual checks use API image export rather than the desktop UI.
final_rule.rule:
1. Payload: write data files next to the model and read them in Revit; do not embed large data in scripts.
2. Floors: Floor.Create accepts several disjoint CurveLoops as one floor (2024); verify HOST_AREA_COMPUTED against the source area in the same call; a Revit floor always has thickness, so tag it as a stand-in.
3. Envelopes as DirectShape: TessellatedShapeBuilder with Target AnyGeometry + Fallback Mesh; read GetGeometricalObjects() exactly once; name with SetName(); store the source id in ApplicationDataId and Mark.
4. Before building envelopes, count edge use in the source triangles: open or non-manifold edges predict Mesh/Sheet outcomes; report volume only for closed solids.
5. Grids: datums carry no Comments; identify grids by a unique name prefix and verify by name. Create arcs with Grid.Create(doc, Arc). To replace a grid set that reuses names, delete and create in one transaction.
6. Grid logic: one grid domain per building wing (standard bays with rational end bays), curved buildings as radial lines plus concentric arcs; never one grid per bounding box. Check that no grid crosses another building or another wing of the same building.
7. Parameter writes: avoid get_Parameter(...)?.Set(...) where the tag matters; a null parameter must fail loudly.
8. Visual checks: prefer Document.ExportImage of a dedicated view (no template, CropBoxActive = false) over driving the desktop; do not use open-application on a running Revit.
9. Scope boxes cannot be created through the API: report legibility of dense site views as a UI task for the user.
final_rule.validation: Counts per stage equal the package (levels, floors, envelopes, grids); floor area equals the source area per floor (here max 0.001 sq ft); envelope bounding boxes equal the source (0.0 ft); closed envelopes' volumes equal the source signed volume; grids read back by name with 0.0 ft endpoint/radius deviation; geometric checks for grid lines crossing other buildings and other wings return 0; an exported plan image is checked before reporting.

notes: Measured build performance (Revit 2024, laptop): 8 levels 0.3 s; 48 floors 2.1 s; 12 envelopes 0.05 s; 5,907-triangle envelope 0.37 s; 361 grids incl. delete 1.3 s. Failure pattern candidates: (a) 'Opening a running desktop app starts a second instance' (desktop-control layer, not the Revit API); (b) 'Null-conditional parameter write silently skips a tag' (get_Parameter returns null for a parameter the category does not have; ?. hides it; related to FP05 and FP31). TessellatedShapeBuilderResult.GetNumberOfIssues was assumed and does not exist in 2024 (FP40 evidence). The decomposition and grid-generation scripts used for the domain grids are kept with the owner; the upstream reading of the source belongs to USG, not ARPL. No client data: the masterplan is the contributor's own design.
